author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
commentary: ननु 'बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसीति' (२-३९) बुद्धिपदोक्तयुद्धाख्यकर्मणोऽपि ज्ञानार्थत्वमुक्तमिति चेत् । तर्हि व्यामिश्रेण क्वचित्कर्मप्रशंसा क्वचिज्ज्ञानप्रशंसेत्येवम्, यद्वा युद्धस्य क्वचित्स्वर्गार्थत्वं क्वचिज्ज्ञानार्थत्वमित्येवं व्यामिश्रेण सन्देहोत्पादकेन वाक्येन मे बुद्धिं मोहयसीव डोलायमानां करोषीव । यदि कामिनो युद्धं स्वर्गार्थं अकामिनो ज्ञानार्थं इति चेत्तथाऽपि यतिधर्म एव नियोगो युक्तो न तु वैकल्पिके युद्धे । अतो येनाहं श्रेयोऽवाप्युयां, तदेकं निश्चित्य वदेति ॥ ३.२॥
translation:
With these simply perplexing words thou seemest to confuse my understanding; therefore, tell me with certainty that one thing by which may reach the highest good. 
V. Perplexing words: --Statements now in praise of action, now of knowledge; or something declaring Svarga as the fruit of this terrible action, sometimes knowledge as its fruit. With such words calculated to bewilder me it doubt, Thou makest my judgement vacillate. If men haunted by desires (ambition) should go to Svarga by fighting and if by the same 'act those destitute of desires should attain knowledge, still it is fit that I should be put in the way of the ascetic, but not asked to try the optional course of blood-shed and cruelty, so that I way surely up the highest good.
The appellation Janadarna in verse (1) according to the Puranic Nirukti means one who has no birth and puts an end to the birth of other beings." So, It is an appropriate address in the present context. (2)
1. "True, all the duties enjoined upon men of the first three orders may, according as they are impelled or not by desires, divide themselves into two classes as Kamya and Akamya; whereas the virtues of devotion, &c., to be practised by the ascetic are purely  Akamya, i.e., such as are not impelled by desires nor attended by the painful results of falling into hell and other suffering as the cruel deeds of war may entail. But the ascetic duties are only intended for those who are ineligible for other duties: and thou belongest to the rank of Janaka, Priyavrata and other souls of high eligibility. Hence, on the principle explained in verste 38, thou shouldst regard pleasure and pain equal, and from doing duties with devotion, duties naturally devolving upon thee, thou shouldst see no evil arises, and, therefore thou deservest to be commanded to go to war, optional as the course may be for others."
